about: Part of the reference catalogue: designed experiments from chapters 2 to 7 of Davies (ed.), The Design and Analysis
of Industrial Experiments, for testing that software reproduces them. source: the citation, with what was read and
when. experiments: each worked example with data (factors, responses, runs exactly as printed, in the printed
order), where it is printed, and expected: every number the book prints for it, as printed text (with a period
for the book's raised decimal point), with where it is printed (a page and a quotation) and check: how to
recompute it, or manual, the reason it is not recomputed. A check with a disagreement records a number known not
to reproduce and why, usually the book's own rounding. not_captured: what in these chapters is not an experiment
tests/test_reference_catalogue.py recomputes every number that has a check.

source.title: The Design and Analysis of Industrial Experiments
source.edition: 2nd edition (1956), reprinted with corrections 1978; the 1979 reprint
source.publisher: Longman Group Limited, London and New York, for Imperial Chemical Industries Limited
source.cite: Davies, O. L. (ed.) (1956), The Design and Analysis of Industrial Experiments, 2nd edition, Longman for ICI
source.read: 2026-10-14, from scans of pp. i-xiii and 1-286 (chapters 1 to 7) of the 1979 reprint; every number copied by hand and checked against the totals the book prints; two tables printed sideways (4-1 and 5-6) taken from their reprints in the appendices, and Table 4-3 read from the page image
source.rights: The book is protected by copyright (© 1956 Imperial Chemical Industries Limited) and is not reproduced here. This file holds facts it reports (numbers, layouts, data) and short quotations that locate each one, for citation and for checking software. The MIT licence of process-improve does not extend to them.

2.5 (numbers of observations: primers for explosives, the Hydrox device, polar blasting gelatine): sample-size calculations, no data
Table 2-4 (p. 19): means of three preparations by each method, not their analyses
chapter 3 (pp. 57-98): sequential tests; the data of Tables 3-2, 3-4 and 3-9 and the fibre differences of p. 73 are inputs to sequential probability ratio tests, which no check computes
Appendix 2A and Appendices 3A to 3C: theory and tables of probabilities, no experiments
6.5 to 6.8 (lattice squares, pp. 220-229): symbolic, no data
Appendix 6A (pp. 230-235): a list of balanced incomplete block designs, not yet held as designs
Appendix 6C (pp. 245-247): the tyre data of Example 6-1 worked again by the missing-value method; the exact results are checked under davies-tyre-road-test
Tables 7-4, 7-6 and 7-8 and Appendices 7A to 7D: notation, sign tables and expectations of mean squares, no data
